Inventory management system
1) Scanning inventory
a) System Shall print a label with identifier for each type of Item.
b) System shall register item being scanned and update the appropriate
database tables with the data of items scanned into inventory.
2) Updating inventory
a) System shall keep counts of items being sold.
b) System shall send end of day reports for current counts of all items in stock.
3) Ordering new Stock
a) System shall provide report of low stock items.
b) System shall receive approval then place order with vendors.
c) System shall predict increase demand based on archived data.
Customer Retention System
1) Enrolling a customer
a) System shall obtain customer information.
b) System shall send out a confirmation email.
c) System shall assign an unique customer ID
2) Send promotions.
a) System shall send promo to customer email if applicable.
b) System shall send promo for customer birthday.
c) System shall send promo if customer had not been in shop after specified
amount time.
3) Update customer profile
a) System shall update customer profile each time customer buys ice-cream.
b) System shall log the type of ice cream that user likes to buy.

column2: Windows 10 Personal Computer

column1: Darwhin Gomez

This Instructional manual is intended for individuals with basic and rudimentary knowledge of personal computers and the Microsoft Windows Operating System. This includes being able to perform simple hardware replacements and additions if needed.
Table of Contents
Background …………………………………..p 1
Tools and Components……………………….p 2
Procedures……………………………………p 4
Installing the Drives………..………..p 4
Configuring RAID 5  .………………p 5-7
References…………………………………..p 8
Background
Our computer systems depend on storage devices to store data for future use. Like many aspects of computing
column2: storage devices have their limits (size
column3: and speed). In order to surpass those limits a new technology was introduced. RAID or as it is formally known Redundant Arrays of Independent Disks allows for the use of multiple storage volumes to be configured as one. This provides the benefit of expanded storage volume as well as other benefits. The benefits differ among the diverse types of RAID arrays
column4: RAID 0 offers more volume and faster writing speeds. RAID 1 offers data redundancy through mirror copies and RAID 5 offers boosts to writing speeds
column5: data redundancy as well as expanded storage.

column1: RAID 5 can provide these benefits through a process known as striping with parity.  This means that the write head stripes information across multiple disks in order to increase speed.  RAID 5 then incorporates the use of a parity bit. With the parity bits in a RAID 5 volume
column2: it is possible to rebuild data in the event of a hard drive malfunction.  It is therefore easy to understand why RAID 5 volumes are an exceedingly popular option when configuring storage arrays in todays computing world.

column1: This manual aims to teach you how to install and configure a RAID 5 array using 3 HDDs. The Manual assumes that you have basic computer skills and are capable of following step by step directions. RAID is a highly effective way of providing redundancy in data storage or increasing performance when reading and writing to storage. There are many distinct types or levels of RAID
column2: this manual will focus on RAID 5. This manual will not cover installing and configuring RAID in a server environment
column3: in addition this manual does not cover installing RAID in other operating systems other than windows ten. There will be two procedures to install and configure our RAID array. The first will be physically installing our hard drives in our system
column4: The second would be configuring our RAID 5 array in our BIOS-UEFI settings. Please follow the directions exactly in the order they are presented.

column1: Key Terms:
There are some key terms that you may want to become familiar before you advance with the procedures. They are:

BIOS/ UEFI- Both BIOS and UEFI are forms of software that kickstart the hardware of your computer before your operating system loads. UEFI is an update to traditional BIOS that supports larger hard drives
column2: quicker boot times
column4: and more graphics and mouse cursor options.

column1: Parity- Is an extra bit of information used to detect errors in storage or ram.
Redundant Array of Inexpensive Disks (RAID)- A collection of HDDS in a storage system that can be configured to provides faster performance
column2: data redundancy

column1: Storage - Describes where information is stored in a computer system in a non-volatile form
column2: typically a Hard Disk Drive
column4: etc.

column1: Striping- is form of writing to a RAID. array in which information is written sequentially between the disks in the array to increase performance. This is also called R.A.I.D. 0 and requires a minimum of two disks.
Mirroring- is a form of writing to a RAID. array in which the information is mirrored between the disks being used
column2: this provides data redundancy or fault tolerance. This is called RAID 1 and requires a minimum of two disks.

column1: RAID 5- This version of RAID. allows for Striping with Parity
column2: this array allows for better speed while providing data redundancy as well. RAID. 5 requires a minimum of three disks to implement.  RAID 5 is also known as Striping with Parity.

column1: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)- A   common storage device that consists of magnetic platters on a spindle that can be written to and read from in computer systems.
Electric Static Discharge (ESD) - The ESD occurs when differently charged objects are brought close together
column2: often creating a visible spark.

column1: Tools and Components
Intel Windows 10 PC
3 SATA HDD (same brand
column2: model

column1: 3 SATA DATA CABLES
3 SATA POWER CABLES
ESD bracelet
Non-Magnetized PC screwdriver kit
Procedures
As mentioned earlier there are two procedures
column2: procedure I must be completed before procedure II.  All steps must be completed in the order presented.  Lets get started!

column1: Installing the drives
Hold down the power button on your PC for five second to turn it off and drain any residual power in the system.
Unplug the power cord from the back of your PC.
Remove the side panel of your PC case to gain access
Note:  Your case may have screws or latches that need to be undone.
Put on your ESD bracelet and attach the opposite end to the PC case to ground yourself.
Caution:
Not properly grounding yourself can result in catastrophic damage to electrical components as a result of ESD.
Align and place HDDs in the drive bays
Use your demagnetized screwdriver to fasten any screws needed for your HDDs.
Connect SATA DATA Cables to your HDDs.
Connect the other end of SATA data cables to your SATA interface on your motherboard.
Connect SATA power cables to your HDDs.
Note: Your power supply may have included SATA cables if that is the case just Use these cables to provide power to your HDDs.
Connect SATA power cables to your power Supply (Skip if you used cables from your power supply.)
Place side panel of your case back on
column2: fasten or screw accordingly.

column1: Plug in your power cord to the back of the PC.
Power on your PC.
Congratulations you have complete the physical installation of your RAID Array
column2: now we just need to Configure it in your BIOS!

column1: Configuring RAID 5
Restart your PC and hold the F2 key to load into the BIOS/UEFI.
Open the System Configuration tab.
Figure :  BIOS MENU with the SATA operations tab opened.
Select Sata Operation.
Toggle RAID
On.
Click Apply.
Click Exit this will cause a system restart.
A prompt will appear instructing you to press the Ctrl and I keys simultaneously.
Using your keyboards arrow keys to navigate select option 1(Create new RAID volume) Press the ENTER key
Figure : RAID MENU showing three non RAID disk
Now the Create Volume MENU has opened.
In the Name Field enter the name you would like for your RAID array. When done press ENTER to cycle to the next field.
Use the Up and Down arrow keys to cycle through the RAID levels Select RAID5 (Parity) press ENTER to cycle to the next field.
Select the desired strip size (I recommend 64 KB) When done press ENTER to cycle to the next field.
The capacity field is pre-set to the maximum capacity using the selected disks
column2: press ENTER to confirm and cycle to the next field.

column1: Double check that that you filled out all the fields correctly
column2: when you are all set press ENTER.

column1: A Warning will inform you that any data on the disks will be lost because you are about to format those disks for a RAID array. Press Y
to confirm.
Congratulations
column2: you have successfully created a RAID 5 array on an Intel Windows 10 PC! The array name will now be displayed along with it’s RAID level
column4: strip size
column5: and status. You can exit the Menu by navigating to option 6 (EXIT) and pressing ENTER.

column1: Comments:
There are settings that can be set to your specific preference like strip size or volume name.  I encourage you to do so
column2: while I like my strip size to be 64KB this might not be the best option for you.  There are different and more advance RAID configurations that were not discussed
column3: I implore you do additional research if you have further interest in RAID.
